project:paradigmas.content:
# Programming paradigms

![Programming paradigms](/images/PLaS/proyectos/lenguajes/lenguajes_0.webp)

## Description

The **Programming Paradigms** website brings together educational content on this subject. The materials have been developed collaboratively by students of the *Programming Languages* course at Universidad Nacional de Colombia, who contribute to it semester after semester.

The site offers theoretical and practical information on several paradigms:

- Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)
- Functional Programming
- Logic Programming
- Parallel Programming
- Concurrent Programming
- Aspect-Oriented Programming (AOP)

Besides the basic concepts and their explanation, it includes tutorials on representative languages for each paradigm.

project:uncode.summary: A tool for learning programming and automatically grading programming exercises. UNCode supports many programming languages, such as Python, Java, C and C++, as well as hardware description languages and Jupyter notebooks.
project:uncode.content:
# UNCode

![UNCode](/images/PLaS/proyectos/proyecto1.svg)

## Description

**UNCode** is a tool for learning programming and automatically grading programming exercises. It supports many languages, such as Python, Java, C and C++, hardware description languages (Verilog and VHDL), and assignments solved in Jupyter notebooks.

The platform uses a grading system based on INGInious: flexible, secure, scalable and configurable to each course's goals. After every submission, students receive automatic feedback.

### Feedback

Learning support combines **summative** and **formative** assessment:

- **Summative:** a numerical grade for the submission.
- **Formative:** help with syntax, semantics, code maintainability and custom tests.

### Platform features

- Linter with good-practice suggestions
- Execution visualizer (Python Tutor)
- Custom input/output testing environment
- Code templates for assignments
- Interactive statistical reports for instructors and students
- Assignment creation wizard, problem bank, manual grading and plagiarism reports

project:analytics.summary: Learning analytics draws on the large amount of data generated in educational settings to make decisions that improve teaching and learning. This project relates learning-process metrics to academic performance in an introductory programming course using mixed methods.

links.context: Edna Johanna Chaparro Amaya · Master's student in Systems and Computing Engineering, Universidad Nacional de Colombia · Email: edchaparroa@unal.edu.co

project:analytics.content:
# Learning Analytics

![Learning Analytics](/images/PLaS/proyectos/proyecto2.webp)

## Description

Learning analytics uses the data generated in educational settings to improve teaching and learning. In programming courses these applications are often effective at guiding interventions; however, many rely only on quantitative data and leave aside qualitative approaches and mixed methods.

### Goal

To determine the relationships between learning-process metrics and academic performance in the *Computer Programming* course, through an analytics strategy grounded in **mixed methods**.

### Methodology

We used an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design:

1. Data preparation and metric design
2. Quantitative and qualitative analysis
3. Identification of relationships with academic performance

We obtained **55 variables** describing the learning process (submissions, verdict rates, software metrics on the code, and use of platform tools).

### Results

- The number of submissions, the success rate and the number of correct and incorrect answers correlate positively with performance.
- Students who failed the course used UNCode more as an automatic grading tool; those who passed used it more to get feedback.

### Keywords

Learning analytics · Computer programming · Mixed methods · Correlation analysis · Academic performance

### Authors

**Edna Johanna Chaparro Amaya**  
Master's student in Systems and Computing Engineering  
Universidad Nacional de Colombia  
Email: [edchaparroa@unal.edu.co](mailto:edchaparroa@unal.edu.co)

project:gamificacion.content:
# Assessing the effect of computer-assisted gamification on the motivation of computer programming students

*Original title (Spanish): Evaluación del efecto de la gamificación asistida por computador en la motivación de los estudiantes de programación de computadores*

![Computer-assisted gamification in a programming course](/images/PLaS/proyectos/proyecto3.webp)

## Description

Teaching and learning Computer Programming poses challenges that call for methodologies in which students take an active role. Game-related methodologies, including **gamification** (the use of game elements in non-game contexts), are studied for their possible effect on motivation, participation, performance and engagement.

Computer-assisted gamified environments have been integrated into programming courses; qualitative findings tend to be positive, while several quantitative analyses find no statistically significant effects. More empirical evidence is needed.

### Goal

To study the effect of computer-assisted gamification on the **motivation to learn** of Computer Programming students.

### Method

- Selection of **CodeGym** as the gamified environment (literature review and comparative analysis)
- **Quasi-experimental** study with an educational intervention
- Measurement with the **MSLQ-Colombia** questionnaire and a perception survey
- **48 students** in two control groups and one experimental group (convenience sampling)

### Results

In the experimental group, the levels associated with *task value* (importance, usefulness, and liking of or interest in the course topics) increased significantly.

### Keywords

Gamification · Computer programming · Gamified environments · Learning motivation

### Related publication

K.D. Cuervo-Cely, J.J. Ramírez-Echeverry, F. Restrepo-Calle (2020). *Computer-Assisted Gamification In A Computer Programming Course: An Experience Report*. ICERI 2020, pp. 6006–6015.

project:vpl.content:
# Assessing the impact of an automated assessment tool on the learning motivation of computer programming students

*Original title (Spanish): Evaluación del impacto en la motivación en el aprendizaje de los estudiantes de programación de computadores mediante el uso de una herramienta de evaluación automática*

![Automated assessment with VPL](/images/PLaS/proyectos/proyecto4.webp)

## Description

In engineering, and particularly in computer science, programming is a core competency. These courses develop the ability to solve problems, write programs, define functions, debug and choose suitable control structures, skills that are also in demand in the workplace.

### Goal

To determine the impact of an **automated source-code assessment** tool on the learning motivation of Computer Programming students at U Compensar university.

### Method

- **Quasi-experimental** study integrating automated assessment into an Algorithms course
- Selection of **VPL** (*Virtual Programming Lab*) after a literature review
- Control and experimental groups
- Measurement with **MSLQ-Colombia**
- **42 participating students**

### Analysis approach

The MSLQ data reveal changes in motivation, while the tool's logs provide evidence about attempts, progress and coding while solving exercises.

### Keywords

Automated assessment · Computer programming · Learning motivation

project:she.summary: SHE (Software Hardening Environment) is a tool for developing fault-tolerant software: it designs software-based fault-tolerance techniques and applies them to programs automatically and selectively.

links.context: Available at the Fault Tolerance Lab (Universidad de Alicante, Spain).

project:she.content:
# SHE: Software Hardening Environment

![SHE: Software Hardening Environment](/images/PLaS/proyectos/proyecto11.webp)

## Description

**SHE** (*Software Hardening Environment*) is a tool for developing fault-tolerant software. It makes it possible to design and implement software-based fault-tolerance techniques and apply them to programs automatically.

The *hardening* (protection) strategy relies on low-level (assembly) code transformation rules. Techniques can be applied **selectively**, protecting only the critical parts of the program: this reduces overheads and gives designers flexibility to balance the system's requirements.

It is cross-platform (tested on GNU/Linux and Windows).

### Supported microprocessors

- Xilinx PicoBlaze 8-bit (KCPSM3)
- Xilinx PicoBlaze 8-bit (KCPSM6)
- Texas Instruments MSP430 16-bit
- *Coming soon:* ARM and RISC-V

### Try it online

Available at the Fault Tolerance Lab of Universidad de Alicante (Spain).

project:ftxac.summary: Higher integration in semiconductor devices has made integrated circuits more susceptible to radiation-induced faults. FTxAC uses approximate computing to design fault-tolerant embedded systems with lower overheads than traditional redundancy.
project:ftxac.content:
# FTxAC

![FTxAC](/images/PLaS/proyectos/proyecto12.webp)

## Description

Higher integration levels in semiconductors have made circuits more susceptible to **radiation-induced faults**. Software, hardware or hybrid mitigation techniques usually impose significant overheads in area, energy and performance.

**FTxAC** explores the **approximate computing** paradigm to propose a systematic strategy for designing radiation-tolerant embedded systems, reducing those overheads compared with the redundancy of traditional approaches.

### Results / publications

- A. Aponte-Moreno, F. Restrepo-Calle and C. Pedraza. *FTxAC: Leveraging the Approximate Computing Paradigm…* IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computing, 2021. doi: [10.1109/TETC.2020.2986235](https://doi.org/10.1109/TETC.2020.2986235)
- A. Aponte-Moreno, F. Restrepo-Calle, C. Pedraza. *Using Approximate Computing and Selective Hardening…* Electronics, 2019.
- A. Aponte-Moreno, F. Restrepo-Calle and C. Pedraza. *A Low-Overhead Radiation Hardening Approach…* RADECS 2019.
- A. Aponte-Moreno, C. Pedraza and F. Restrepo-Calle. *Reducing Overheads in Software-based Fault Tolerant Systems…* LATS 2019. doi: [10.1109/LATW.2019.8704586](https://doi.org/10.1109/LATW.2019.8704586)
- A. Aponte-Moreno et al. *A review of approximate computing techniques towards fault mitigation…* LATS 2018. doi: [10.1109/LATW.2018.8347241](https://doi.org/10.1109/LATW.2018.8347241)

project:transito.summary: Adding variables on road crashes and road infrastructure problems taken from social networks and mobility apps can improve estimates of where crashes occur, compared with models based only on official crash data.
project:transito.content:
# Road crash prediction model

![Road crash prediction model](/images/PLaS/proyectos/proyecto13.webp)

## Description

Adding variables on crashes and road infrastructure taken from **social networks** and mobility apps can improve estimates of crash occurrence, compared with models that use only official crash data.

The project seeks to identify variables that contribute to a more complete model of crash probability in a city like **Bogotá**.

### Results / publications

Camilo Gutierrez-Osorio; Cesar Augusto Pedraza. *Characterizing road accidents in urban areas of Bogota (Colombia): A data science approach*. 2019 2nd Latin American Conference on Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS LATAM). IEEE.

project:maleza.summary: This project develops software to quantify weeds in vegetable crops in Colombian farming areas from multispectral images, so that herbicides can be applied more precisely.
project:maleza.content:
# Weed quantification in vegetable crops

![Weed quantification in vegetable crops](/images/PLaS/proyectos/proyecto14.jpg)

## Description

The goal is to develop software that **quantifies weeds** in vegetable crops in Colombian farming areas from **multispectral images**.

This technology is expected to locate more precisely where to apply herbicides, improving economic efficiency and bringing environmental and health benefits.
